extracted.intended_audience: web developers/site authors and accessibility engineers implementing MathJax for screenreader/assistive-technology users
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for installing, configuring, and using the MathJax Accessibility Extensions (accessibility-menu, explorer, auto-collapse, collapsible, semantic-enrich, mathjax-sre) to provide accessible speech and exploration of math on webpages. Covers configuration options, keyboard navigation, compatibility, and known support issues across browsers and screenreaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provided extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: List of accessibility extensions: accessibility-menu.js, explorer.js, auto-collapse.js, collapsible.js, semantic-enrich.js, mathjax-sre.js (custom build of speech-rule-engine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These extensions provide features such as a lightweight accessibility menu, speech-text generation, expression exploration/highlighting, responsive collapsing, semantic enrichment, and a speech-rule engine. They are the core pieces to enable accessible rendering and exploration of equations.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathJax version requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The extensions require MathJax v2.6 or higher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Version 2.7.0 included the Accessibility Menu Extension in combined configuration files; for MathJax v2.6, load the extensions from a v2.7 distribution. Note repeated elsewhere as a hard dependency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quick start / Activation via accessibility-menu
rubrics_metrics.description: Add the Accessibility Menu Extension (a11y/accessibility-menu.js) to MathJax configuration before loading MathJax.js to give users an opt-in menu for accessibility features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By default the Accessibility Menu only extends the MathJax Menu with options; it does not load other extensions unless configured or the user opts in. Example config snippet is provided. You may also pre-load sub-extensions directly in the extensions array or enable them via menuSettings.

rubrics_metrics.name: menuSettings toggles (collapsible, autocollapse, explorer)
rubrics_metrics.description: menuSettings contains options: collapsible (false/true), autocollapse (false/true), explorer (false/true).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If collapsible is true, it loads/enables collapsible.js. If autocollapse is true, it loads/enables auto-collapse.js. If explorer is true, it loads/enables explorer.js. Defaults are false; example configuration shows how to enable them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explorer extension features
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides sub-expression exploration tools: highlighting, top-level speech-text generation (aria-label), and an application for accessible keyboard navigation with synchronized highlighting and speech-text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Explorer is the largest piece and supports hover/permanent highlighting, aria-label generation for outer elements, and a walker application for exploring subexpressions visually and aurally. It modifies MathML and can re-render output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explorer walker modes (none/syntactic/semantic)
rubrics_metrics.description: walker (none, syntactic, semantic) specifies rules for the exploration tool; default 'syntactic'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The semantic mode tries to group sub-expressions into meaningful parts (e.g., plus and the following summand together). Choice affects how navigation groups and presents subexpressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explorer highlighting options (none/hover/flame)
rubrics_metrics.description: highlight specifies highlighting of sub-expression complexity: 'none', 'hover', or 'flame'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'hover' highlights on pointer hover; 'flame' uses background opacity to indicate complexity (useful with collapsed expressions). Background/foreground colors are configurable to control highlight appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight color selection (background/foreground)
rubrics_metrics.description: background and foreground options choose highlight colors (background: blue, red, green, yellow, cyan, magenta, white, black; foreground: black, white, magenta, cyan, yellow, green, red, blue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These colors are used for highlighting and when using the walker to explore an expression; pick combinations for sufficient contrast and visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explorer speech controls (speech, generation, subtitle, ruleset)
rubrics_metrics.description: speech (true/false) controls whether speech-text is generated; generation (eager, mixed, lazy) controls level of detail in top-level speech; subtitle (true/false) controls whether subtitles with speech text are shown; ruleset selects speech-rule set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ruleset options include mathspeak-default/brief/sbrief and chromevox-default/short/alternative. Use 'lazy' for short summaries by default; enabling speech will add aria-labels and synchronized speech during exploration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyboard navigation keybindings and behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Key bindings: SHIFT+SPACE start (requires focus), ESC stop (resumes where left off), UP/DOWN move up/down tree (down starts at left-most at level), LEFT/RIGHT navigate horizontally, ENTER toggle collapsed state of current sub-expression and regenerate speech-text, SPACE get positional information (current level, collapsibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes about implementation quality: some browser/screenreader/OS combinations require disabling screenreader 'browse' modes (NVDA browse mode, JAWS virtual cursor) before launching. The application plays an aural earcon at top/bottom; behavior persists across restarts (continues where left off). See configuration and support sections for more keyboard behavior details.

rubrics_metrics.name: auto-collapse behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: auto-collapse.js automatically collapses sub-expressions so the equation fits the viewport width and reacts to viewport changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: auto-collapse will automatically load collapsible.js. The extension only offers a configuration option to disable it (auto-collapse: { disabled: false }).

rubrics_metrics.name: collapsible behavior and complexity metric
rubrics_metrics.description: collapsible.js generates a complexity metric (using semantic enrichment) and inserts elements allowing expressions to be collapsed by user clicking, based on that metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by auto-collapse.js and explorer.js. Only configuration option is to disable collapsible (collapsible: { disabled: false }). The complexity metric is used for deciding collapsibility and for highlighting opacity when 'flame' highlight is selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: semantic enrichment embedding
rubrics_metrics.description: semantic-enrich.js coordinates creation and embedding of semantic information (from mathjax-sre) into MathJax output for use by other extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the semantic info used by collapsible and explorer for grouping and complexity metrics. Only configuration option is to disable semantic-enrich ({ disabled: false }).

rubrics_metrics.name: mathjax-sre role (speech-rule-engine)
rubrics_metrics.description: mathjax-sre.js is a custom build of speech-rule-engine providing semantic analysis of MathML and speech-text generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It provides the semantic enrichment and speech generation backend used by semantic-enrich and explorer; files include the components of speech-rule-engine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with AssistiveMML
rubrics_metrics.description: When Accessibility Extension speech generation is active, the extension will disable the AssistiveMML extension (auto-loaded with MathJax v2.6+); otherwise, some screenreaders may read math twice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a page author configures the accessibility extensions to always produce speech text, they should disable AssistiveMML to avoid double reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-rendering side-effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Enabling these extensions triggers a re-rendering of output as the underlying MathML is modified to reflect semantic analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can lead to small visual changes (e.g., properly matching fence sizes). Be aware that enabling extensions may change layout/appearance slightly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported MathJax output formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Explorer only works with MathJax's CommonHTML, SVG, and HTML-CSS output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While extensions generally work with any MathJax setup, the Explorer's keyboard/navigation features depend on these output formats. Note MathJax v2.6+ is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Browser support expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Support focused on maintained browsers: IE 10+ and Edge, Chrome, Safari, Firefox. Cannot support IE9 and below due to severe browser bugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Older versions of browsers (except IE) should generally work. Specific behavioral issues vary by browser+screenreader combinations — consult the support/test-results section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile support limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic voicing (via aria-labels) should work with Apple VoiceOver and Android TalkBack. The Explorer tool does not support sub-expression exploration on mobile browsers/touchscreens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mobile: use ARIA-based speech summaries; do not expect keyboard-driven walker/explorer functionality on touch devices yet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screenreader support is variable; test combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Test results vary significantly depending on browser, OS, and screenreader. Not all combinations are usable; good results are expected only when 1 or 2 out of 3 requirements are fixed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A table of results is provided. Authors should test their target combinations rather than assume universal support. Many notes identify specific problems per screenreader-browser-OS combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable screenreader-specific caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain screenreaders have specific limitations: JAWS may not support MathML constructs generated by the extensions (broken speech), ORCA often ignores aria-labels and aria-live regions, WindowEyes can ignore aria-hidden and speak visual output, ChromeVox occasionally reads characters (e.g., 'd i v').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the detailed support table for per-screenreader notes: e.g., JAWS often requires manual Browse/Focus switching, may speak 'empty application', and can break Explorer; ORCA/WindowEyes present severe problems; ChromeVox has generally better results but occasional glitches when exploring quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Browse vs Focus mode interaction and switching
rubrics_metrics.description: Most screenreaders have Browse (virtual) and Focus (forms) modes; users often must switch to Focus mode to interact with the Explorer application. Different screenreaders use different keys to switch (NVDA: NVDA+SPACE; JAWS: JAWS+Z; Window Eyes: CTRL+SHIFT+A; VoiceOver: SHIFT+CTRL+CMD+ARROW; ChromeVox: none; ORCA: ORCA+A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UX problems arise combining browse-mode reading and Explorer interaction: authors should design affordances to let users enter focus on equations (tabindex tracking, explicit focusable elements), but behavior is inconsistent across outputs and screenreaders. After exiting Explorer, users often need to manually return to browse mode; maintaining tabindex/browse position sync is a common challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verbosity / missing and excessive voicing
rubrics_metrics.description: Screenreader verbosity settings can change how elements are announced and how labels are spoken; some screenreaders voice common math symbols via configurable options, others may speak unexpected characters/dashes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WindowEyes offers a configuration for voicing common mathematical symbols (disabled by default). Be aware that different verbosity settings or screenreaders can produce unexpected or excessive verbalizations; test with target users and configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing resources and demos
rubrics_metrics.description: Demos available for testing individual equations (Semantics-Lab/walker) and a real-world demonstration (Struik-speech.html). Videos demonstrate behavior across combinations of browsers/OS/screenreaders. Site is open source with GitHub release packages and README for building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the demos and videos to verify functionality and to observe common authoring mistakes that may reduce accessibility. Pre-built packages available on GitHub releases; building requires Grunt per repository README.
